- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-90+ values), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “reversion to mean” after peaks.
- Model underestimates true mean price levels, especially in the 15–25 day range, suggesting it doesn’t adequately weight recent downward trends.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — true values often dip below forecast before model adjusts.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility, producing erratic forecasts around 10–15 day marks, especially when true values show consolidation or minor reversals.
- Model tends to underestimate true price levels in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, suggesting it underweights recent downward momentum or ignores tail risk.
